Artwork & dialogue notes

Voter Street is an unofficial fictional arcade game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by any party. Its residents, remarks and gameplay scores are invented; they are not real quotations, polling, or a measure of public opinion.

Party artwork

Logos were sourced from the official PA, ANC, DA and EFF websites. Logos remain the identifying marks of their respective parties.

Additional logos: ActionSA, National Coloured Congress (NCC), Freedom Front Plus (FF+), uMkhonto weSizwe (MK), GOOD, and People’s Movement for Change (PMC). Their logos come from their respective websites. New-party dialogue uses original general service-delivery jokes, not attributed allegations.

What informed the remarks?

The writing samples themes in published reporting, mainly around the 2024 election. It does not claim these concerns represent all supporters, or their relative prevalence. English and Afrikaans phrases are shared across randomly assigned characters, independently of skin tone or party.

  • ANC: frustration with unemployment, corruption and services after decades in government. Reuters, 1 June 2024.
  • DA: criticism and internal disagreement about Gaza. Daily Maverick, 18 January 2024. This is disputed political criticism: the DA has also advocated a sovereign Palestinian state and a two-state solution. EWN, 19 January 2024. The game does not establish that the party supports genocide.
  • PA: criticism of rhetoric about migrants and changing coalition relationships. Human Rights Watch, 6 May 2024; Daily Maverick, 6 June 2024. See also the party’s own 2024 manifesto.
  • EFF: questions about delivery and published allegations concerning VBS. The EFF rejected the affidavit allegations as unfounded and misleading; the game’s questions do not assert guilt. SABC, 13 July 2024.

Everyday remarks, loyal catchphrases and jokes about rent, promises and potholes are original fictional writing. Loyal residents and difficulty rules are distributed evenly across the parties.

Scenery

The Camps Bay location is a stylised fictional coastal neighbourhood, not an accurate street map. Music and capture jingles are original synthesized game audio, not party songs. The Table Mountain backdrop is an AI-generated illustration. Ward 50, Ward 60 and Ward 54 are fictional game districts, not reproductions of official ward boundaries. Street scenery, vehicles and characters are original procedural 3D models. Rendering uses Three.js under the MIT licence.

Sources reviewed 22 September 2026.
